A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EchoNeRF paper, including complete Appendices A–G. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, equations, tables, and figures; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments evaluating floorplan reconstruction, RSSI prediction, and robustness in Section 4, Tables 1–2, and Appendices C, D, and F.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original simulation results in Section 4, Tables 1–2, and Appendices C, D, and F.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain identical opacity/orientation modeling, LoS and reflection components, two-stage training, losses, regularization, and implementation procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same Zillow floorplans and Sionna WiFi simulations for floorplan inference, RSSI prediction, and ray tracing. Furniture and location-uncertainty scenarios, including the additional floorplans in Appendix F, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MLP, Heatmap Segmentation, NeRF2, and EchoNeRF_LoS as comparators. The NeWRF and NeRF2 visual comparison in Figure 2 is also identical.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain the same 1000/2000-receiver settings, 80/20 training/test split, model configurations, simulation procedures, and Wall_IoU, F1, and RPE metrics.

E4.justification: The LoS-only ablation, receiver-location sensitivity, furniture examples, reflection-power contribution analysis, and unknown-transmitter experiments are identical in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 retain the same reporting of means and standard deviations across 20 experiments. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains EchoNeRF's Wall_IoU of 0.38 ± 0.06, F1 of 0.55 ± 0.06, and RPE of 3.56 at 2000 receiver locations.

T1.justification: The model equations and gradient reasoning in Section 3, channel-power derivations in Appendices A–B, and transmitter-location likelihood derivation in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about learning floorplans from sparse wireless power measurements and enabling subsequent signal prediction and ray tracing.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning blind spots, missing walls, through-wall simulation, higher-order reflections, furniture, and possible 3D extensions. Appendix G's societal-impact discussion is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains identical architecture, sampling, hyperparameter, optimizer, and NVIDIA A100 details. Both versions state the same plan to release code, data, and baselines upon acceptance.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 42 references are identical, including the positioning relative to wireless channel prediction, neural acoustic fields, and reflection modeling in optical NeRFs.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 28 May 2025 to v2 dated 2 September 2025. The title, authors, prose, section order, and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 15 figures and both tables retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The margin-stamp text update does not change the paper's layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, derivations, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation remain identical throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
